summary: Radha Krishna Choudhary was an Indologist and historian who studied at Tej Narayan Banaili College and Patna University. He headed the history department at Ganesh Dutt College, served as principal of Shankar Sah Vikramshila Mahavidyalaya, and taught at Tilka Manjhi Bhagalpur University.

Radha Kumud Mukherjee (1884–1963) was an Indology and history scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta. He held appointments at Banaras Hindu University (~1916–1917) and the University of Mysore (~1917–1921), including heading the history department at Maharaja's College, Mysore.

Radhika Herzberger is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Toronto in 1982 under the supervision of Bimal Krishna Matilal. Around 1982, she became Director of the Rishi Valley School.

Rafal Stepien is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü and Bernard Faure. He was an Academic Visitor at Wadham College (2012–2013) and an Exchange Scholar at Harvard University (attested 2015).
Rafał Jan Felbur is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued his doctoral studies at Stanford University under Paul Harrison, also studying under John R. McRae and Luis O. Gómez.

Raffaele Torella (born 1950) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Raniero Gnoli. He served as a professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1976–1980) and as a faculty member at Sapienza University of Rome (~1980–2020).
Raffaello Orlando is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Princeton University under doctoral supervisor Denis Twitchett, completing his PhD in 1981.

Raghu Ananthanarayanan studied engineering at IIT Madras and trained in philosophy and religious studies under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya and T. K. V. Desikachar. He taught at Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram and was a visiting faculty member at IIM Ahmedabad.

Raghu Vira (1902–1963) was an Indology, Buddhist, and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who earned degrees from Punjab, London, and Leiden. He founded the International Academy of Indian Culture and headed the Sanskrit department at Sanatan Dharma College (~1934–1946).

Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar (1893–1964) was an Indologist and philosopher. Formerly the principal of Sir Parashurambhau College, he served as a professor and Director of the Post-Graduate and Research Department at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.
Raghunath Giri was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Vamacharana Bhattacharya. He served as a department head at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Rahul Peter Das is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Klaus Ludwig Janert and Albrecht Wezler, earning his D. Phil and Habilitation from Hamburg. He taught at Hamburg, Bonn, Groningen, and Marburg before becoming Professor at Halle-Wittenberg (1994–2020).

Rahul Sankrityayan (1893–1963) was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He held a Sanskrit teaching post at Vidyalankara Pirivena (1927) and taught Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University (1937), where he later held a professorship (1945–1947).

Raimo Anttila (1935–2023) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Yale University under Warren Cowgill from ~1962 to 1966, and later held academic posts at the University of California, Los Angeles (1965) and the University of Helsinki (1971–1976).

Raimon Panikkar (1918–2010) was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned doctorates from Complutense University and Pontifical Lateran University, and he held faculty positions at Complutense (1946–1953), Harvard (1966–1971), and UC Santa Barbara (1971–1978).

Raimond Gaita (born 1946) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Melbourne and the University of Leeds. He served as Professor of Moral Philosophy at King's College London (1977–2011) and Foundation Professor of Philosophy at Australian Catholic University (1993–2011).

Rajan Gurukkal is a historian educated at Calicut University and Jawaharlal Nehru University. He served as Director of the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (1988) and held posts at JNU, Humboldt University, EHESS, and IISc.

Rajendra Chandra Hazra (1904–1982) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka under Sushil Kumar De. He held teaching posts at Jagannath University and the University of Dhaka, and was Associate Professor at Sanskrit College and University (1951–1972).

Rajendralal Mitra (1824–1891) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Medical College, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He directed the Wards' Institution (1856–1881) and served as librarian-cum-assistant-secretary (1846–1856) and later president (1885) of The Asiatic Society.

Rajkrishna Mukhopadhyay (1845–1886) was a historian. He studied at Krishnagar Government College and Presidency University, and later held academic posts at Scottish Church College and Presidency University.
